items.title: Foreign driving licence not valid in India without local authorisation: P&H High Court
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court recently declined to rely on a man's foreign driving licence to exonerate him from his liability in a road accident case [Sameer Gaba v Priyanka & Others] Justice Deepak Gupta noted that Section 3 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 prohibits a person from driving a motor vehicle in a public place unless he holds an effective driving licence authorising him to drive that vehicle. Hence, a foreign driving licence will not be automatically valid in India unless it is endorsed by an Indian authority, the Court said in its verdict of September 7. "A foreign driving licence does not, merely because it is valid in the country of its issuance, automatically confer a right upon its holder to drive a motor vehicle in India," the Court added. The Court was hearing an appeal filed by the driver against an order of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT) at Kurukshetra. The MACT had allowed the concerned insurance company to recover the compensation amount paid by it to a road accident victim's family from the driver who did not possess a valid driving licence in India. items.title: Judiciary not averse to criticism but it must come through appropriate forum: Supreme Court in NCERT textbook case
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently observed that the judiciary is not averse to criticism, but made it clear that such criticism must be voiced through an appropriate forum and not find its way into school curriculum without verification. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the observation while disposing of its suo motu case concerning a chapter titled The Role of the Judiciary in our Society in the NCERT Grade 8 Social Science textbook called Exploring Society: India and Beyond. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana "The Judiciary, as an institution, is not, and cannot be, averse to criticism. Fair, informed and constructive critique of judicial functioning is a legitimate and necessary feature of a vibrant constitutional democracy, contributing to institutional accountability and self-correction. What is required, however, is that such criticism be voiced through the appropriate forum and in a fair, rational mechanism, and not find its way, without verification, into a school curriculum meant for impressionable minds," the Court said in its order. items.summary: YouTuber Ajeet Bharti has approached the Delhi High Court seeking anticipatory bail in the SC/ST Act case registered against him for his comments regarding Chandrashekhar Azad Ravan. items.title: UPSC aspirants write to Rahul Gandhi citing irregularities in 2026 Prelims exam
items.summary: A group of civil aspirants has raised concerns regarding significant irregularities in the Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination, 2026, conducted by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC). In a representation submitted to Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, they state that the General Studies Paper I had "ambiguous, non-conclusive answers, leading to ambiguity in 14 questions, along with wrong answers in the provisional answer key." They further state that the GS Paper II, i.e., CSAT, had "wrong interpretations in 12 questions (10 Reading Comprehensions + 2 Mathematics), thereby compromising the objective nature of the examination." Aspirants have cited the subjectivity of several answers, as well as the mistakes in the UPSC’s provisional answer key, which they say reveals a lack of institutional diligence and accountability. An aspirant from the UPSC accountability forum said, “There are candidates for whom this was the last attempt this year.
